obligations.summary: Member States shall provide SMEs, including start-ups registered or branched in the Union, with priority access to AI regulatory sandboxes, provided they fulfil the eligibility conditions and selection criteria.
exceptions: Priority access shall not preclude other SMEs or start-ups from access to the AI regulatory sandbox if they also fulfil the eligibility conditions and selection criteria.

obligations.summary: Member States shall organise specific awareness raising and training activities on the application of this Regulation tailored to the needs of SMEs, start-ups, deployers, and, as appropriate, local public authorities.

Member States shall utilise existing dedicated channels and, where appropriate, establish new ones to communicate with SMEs, start-ups, deployers, innovators, and local public authorities to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation, including participation in AI regulatory sandboxes.
Member States shall facilitate the participation of SMEs and other relevant stakeholders in the standardisation development process.

When setting fees for conformity assessment under Article 43, the specific interests and needs of SME providers, including start-ups, shall be taken into account by reducing fees proportionately to their size, market size, and other relevant indicators.
The AI Office shall provide standardised templates for areas covered by this Regulation, as specified by the Board in its request.
The AI Office shall develop and maintain a single information platform providing easy-to-use information in relation to this Regulation for all operators across the Union.
The AI Office shall organise appropriate communication campaigns to raise awareness about the obligations arising from this Regulation.
The AI Office shall evaluate and promote the convergence of best practices in public procurement procedures in relation to AI systems.
